A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SiMHand and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references and Appendix Sections 6.1–6.7. Full-page text and rendering comparisons establish that differences are confined to pages 1 and 5.

before.justification: v1 reports original hand pose estimation experiments, quantitative ablations and qualitative results in Section 4 and the appendix, including comparisons with TempCLR and weakly supervised training.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experiments, ablations and qualitative results in Section 4 and the appendix.

M1.justification: The PCA-based positive mining, inverse geometric transformations and adaptively weighted contrastive learning procedure are unchanged. Equation 3 replaces a bar with a tilde on the negative feature, matching its existing definition in v1 rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego4D and 100DOH for pre-training and FreiHand, DexYCB and AssemblyHands for downstream evaluation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed, including in the appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments: the main comparisons retain no pre-training, SimCLR and PeCLR; appendix Tables 5–8 retain TempCLR, weakly supervised training and the same additional hand pose methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendix retain the same splits, sample sizes, augmentations, ResNet-50 configuration, training settings and MPJPE/PCK-AUC evaluation. The limited-label and varying-data-size protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The pre-training and fine-tuning size analyses, adaptive-weighting ablation, Top-K sensitivity study and viewpoint analysis are identical. The appendix retains the same noisy-label comparison and qualitative occlusion and similar-hand analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged across the main text and appendix. For example, Table 1 retains SiMHand's Ego&Exo-2M MPJPE values of 15.79, 16.71 and 18.23 mm on FreiHand, DexYCB and AssemblyHands, respectively.

T1.justification: Equation 3's negative-feature accent changes from a bar to a tilde, consistent with the inverse-transformed feature already defined in Section 3.3 and depicted in Figure 3. This corrects notation without revising mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: mining similar hands from 2.0M images, parameter-free adaptive weighting and improved downstream hand pose estimation. The abstract's word correction does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning sample diversity, viewpoint matching, limited-label benefits, occlusion handling and noisy weak supervision are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Preprocessing, PCA dimensionality, optimizer settings, input resolution, temperatures, batch sizes, GPU information and fine-tuning details remain identical. The code-access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are identical, as is the positioning relative to SimCLR, PeCLR, TempCLR and non-self-positive contrastive learning.

P1.justification: v3 corrects 'sorely' to 'solely' in the abstract and the negative-feature accent in Equation 3, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Paragraphs, terminology, section order and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–8 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. The page layout is unchanged; the version stamp and isolated typographical corrections do not constitute a display redesign.

improvement.justification: The abstract typo and Equation 3 notation correction provide slight local polish, but v1 already defines the intended negative-feature transformation. With the scientific arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and appendices unchanged, these corrections do not establish a meaningful paper-level quality difference.
